progression: Exact current ordinary full-time BSc Natural Sciences 56948, Radboud. Dutch legally controlling 2026–27 OER v1.1, adopted 9 July and amended 6 October 2026, establishes 60 EC first year, 30 EC later shared core, 72 EC specialisation (selected first-listed Physical Chemistry: 33 required plus 39 restricted), 6 EC genuine free electives and 12 EC individual internship: 180 total. No unspecialised route exists; Physical Chemistry is a neutral official-order tie break, not a UCR-fit choice. Biophysics and Biochemistry remain separate alternatives and are not merged. First-listed current choices are MOL136, MOL155, MOL170A, FFIL100, MOL040 and MOL157. Restricted space uses non-overlapping eligible NWI bachelor courses and/or permitted 15–30 EC minor; excluded minors Physical Organic Chemistry, Bio-organic Chemistry and Sustainable Chemistry and listed overlapping combinations apply. The OER reference to Article7.6 for minor exclusions is a cross-reference typo: the actual exclusion list is Article7.7. Prospective 2027–28 web tables instead show 24 shared and 78 specialisation EC; they do not replace current 30/72. Article7.2 designates Dutch although most courses are English, unlike the general English recruitment-page label. First-year MOL0861 Academic Skills is 0 EC inside the later MOL086 3 EC; compulsory RADAr participation/reflection is noncredit. Writing MOL190 requires passed MOL0861. Academic skills completion occurs in the final year, not before research starts. Internship MOL200A requires full B1 plus at least60 later EC (120 total), departmental prior knowledge as checked before MOL200R administrative admission, approved proposal, individual supervised theoretical/practical work and written/oral reports. Project and Sustainability Certificate participation are recorded for the internship. BSA39 EC. Course-specific prior knowledge and laboratory participation remain applicable; no individual elective plan is certified. Old-cohort substitutions and examination-only historical options are not added to the selected current route.

candidateAssessment.label: Life, environmental & quantitative sciences
candidateAssessment.reason: UCR provides substantive biochemistry, molecular biology and laboratory skills, environmental science, mathematics and data analysis. Neither proposed programme sustains the defining physics and chemistry combination of Natural Sciences and the selected Physical Chemistry route. Advanced mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum theory, chemical analysis and synthesis, bonding and physical chemistry remain missing as a coherent sequence. Adding sustainability materials teaching, neuroscience or machine learning does not repair that disciplinary gap. No complete defensible UCR alternative is established. This is a weighted academic judgment, not a demand for identical degrees or professional equivalence.
